page: Amazon Web Services d3.4xlarge is a dense, storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 3.1 GHz, delivering 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is set at 128 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, yielding an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. A primary defining architectural feature is the bundled local storage capacity, consisting of 23,760 GB of dense magnetic hard disk drives (HDD). Network capability features a baseline throughput of 12 Gbps. The instance contains no dedicated hardware accelerators or GPUs.

Benchmark results highlight an architecture oriented toward parallel data throughput rather than single-threaded raw speed. Single-core performance falls into the lower quartile, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1016.0, weak compression throughput, and a stress-ng single-core score of 1327.69. Conversely, multi-threaded operations demonstrate average tier execution, posting a Geekbench multi-core mark of 6503.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 14431.5. Memory throughput remains solid with 86.61 GB/sec uncached reads and 45.38 GB/sec writes, supporting Redis operations reaching 13.67 million operations per second and static web throughput of 11.96 GB/sec.

From a cost efficiency standpoint, the d3.4xlarge delivers economical capacity for massive data footprints compared to high-speed NVMe or memory-centric architectures. The tradeoff lies in the mechanical storage medium, where sequential reads and bulk capacity take precedence over low-latency random IOPS. The processor and memory configuration provides balanced support for managing massive datasets locally. Consequently, the instance is appropriate for distributed file systems, data lakes, Apache Hadoop and Kafka clusters, log processing pipelines, and large sequential data warehousing jobs.
description: Amazon Web Services d3.4xlarge is a storage-optimized instance tailored for high-capacity sequential storage environments. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it features an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor with 16 vCPUs, 8 physical cores, and 128 GB of DDR4 system memory. Its primary asset is 23,760 GB of direct-attached mechanical HDD storage alongside a 12 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results indicate moderate multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth, offset by modest single-threaded compute metrics. The dense HDD capacity makes d3.4xlarge a cost-effective solution for large-scale data storage where high random IOPS is unnecessary, making it suitable for distributed file systems, data lakes, log processing, and big data analytical clusters.
